build_tactics: Closes once, plants, and full-attacks with a two-hander every round until something dies -- usually whatever it swung at. Eats hits rather than reposition; moving costs damage and damage is the whole plan.

boons_detail.description: (Counters Focus Casting) You no longer need to make a check to cast without your focus item, or you ignore part of the Focus Casting penalty; maintaining a sphere ability that needs a standard action to concentrate on requires only a move action.
boons_detail.name: Easy Focus

boons_detail.description: (Pairs with Draining Casting) You shore up your lifeforce against draining magic; you may use Constitution as your casting ability modifier if it is higher than your usual one.
boons_detail.name: Fortified Casting

drawbacks_detail.description: Your magic requires elaborate gestures; you need a free hand and suffer arcane-style spell failure in armor heavier than light. May be taken twice (no armor or shield at all without failure).
drawbacks_detail.name: Somatic Casting

drawbacks_detail.description: Your magic requires expending consumable materials/components worth roughly 1 sp per caster level each time you use a sphere ability.
drawbacks_detail.name: Material Casting

drawbacks_detail.description: Spending a spell point forces a Fortitude save (DC 10 + 1/2 caster level) or you become sickened (then nauseated, then stunned on repeated failures).
drawbacks_detail.name: Painful Magic

drawbacks_detail.description: After resting you must pre-assign your spell points to specific spheres you possess; you may only spend points on the spheres you prepared until you next rest.
drawbacks_detail.name: Prepared Caster

Skill Unlock: Spellcraft.10 Ranks: You can identify magic items without using detect magic, though the DC is increased by 10.
Skill Unlock: Spellcraft.15 Ranks: Identifying magic items is a standard action, and learning a spell takes 1 minute per spell level.
Skill Unlock: Spellcraft.20 Ranks: When attempting a caster level check, you can attempt a Spellcraft check at -20 against the same DC; success grants a +2 circumstance bonus.
Skill Unlock: Spellcraft.5 Ranks: Identifying magic items takes 1 full round, and the time to learn a spell from a spellbook is halved.

armored confidence (ex).description: while wearing armor, the fighter gains a bonus on intimidate checks based upon the type of armor he is wearing: +1 for light armor, +2 for medium armor, or +3 for heavy armor. This bonus increases by 1 at 7th level and every 4 fighter levels thereafter, to a maximum of +4 at 19th level. In addition, the fighter adds half his armored confidence bonus to the dc of intimidate checks to demoralize him.

critical deflection (ex).description: while wearing armor or using a shield, the fighter gains a +2 bonus to his ac against attack rolls made to confirm a critical hit. This bonus increases by 1 at 7th level and every 4 fighter levels thereafter, to a maximum of +6 at 19th level.

steel headbutt (ex).description: while wearing medium or heavy armor, a fighter can deliver a headbutt with his helm as part of a full attack action. This headbutt is in addition to his normal attacks, and is made using the fighters base attack bonus -5. A helmet headbutt deals 1d3 points of damage if the fighter is wearing medium armor, or 1d4 points of damage if he is wearing heavy armor (1d2 and 1d3, respectively, for small creatures), plus an amount of damage equal to 1/2 the fighters strength modifier. Treat this attack as a weapon attack made using the same special material (if any) as the armor. The armors enhancement bonus does not modify the headbutt attack, but the helm can be enchanted as a separate weapon.

trained initiative (ex).description: as long as he is wielding a weapon from the associated weapon group or is able to draw such a weapon, the fighter applies his weapon training bonus to initiative checks.

trained throw (ex).description: when the fighter makes a ranged attack with a thrown weapon and applies his dexterity modifier on attack rolls and his strength modifier on damage rolls, he doubles his weapon training bonus on damage rolls.

class_ability_desc.armor mastery: At 19th level, a fighter gains DR 5/- whenever he is wearing armor or using a shield.
class_ability_desc.armor training: Starting at 3rd level, a fighter learns to be more maneuverable while wearing armor. Whenever he is wearing armor, he reduces the armor check penalty by 1 (to a minimum of 0) and increases the maximum Dexterity bonus allowed by his armor by 1. Every four levels thereafter (7th, 11th, and 15th), these bonuses increase by +1 each time, to a maximum -4 reduction of the armor check penalty and a +4 increase of the maximum Dexterity bonus allowed. In addition, a fighter can also move at his normal speed while wearing medium armor. At 7th level, a fighter can move at his normal speed while wearing heavy armor.
class_ability_desc.bonus feats: At 1st level, and at every even level thereafter, a fighter gains a bonus feat in addition to those gained from normal advancement (meaning that the fighter gains a feat at every level). These bonus feats must be selected from those listed as combat feats, sometimes also called "fighter bonus feats."Upon reaching 4th level, and every four levels thereafter (8th, 12th, and so on), a fighter can choose to learn a new bonus feat in place of a bonus feat he has already learned. In effect, the fighter loses the bonus feat in exchange for the new one. The old feat cannot be one that was used as a prerequisite for another feat, prestige class, or other ability. A fighter can only change one feat at any given level and must choose whether or not to swap the feat at the time he gains a new bonus feat for the level.
class_ability_desc.bravery: Starting at 2nd level, a fighter gains a +1 bonus on Will saves against fear. This bonus increases by +1 for every four levels beyond 2nd.
class_ability_desc.weapon mastery: At 20th level, a fighter chooses one weapon, such as the longsword, greataxe, or longbow. Any attacks made with that weapon automatically confirm all critical threats and have their damage multiplier increased by 1 (×2 becomes ×3, for example). In addition, he cannot be disarmed while wielding a weapon of this type. Alternate Capstones
class_ability_desc.weapon training: Starting at 5th level, a fighter can select one group of weapons, as noted below. Whenever he attacks with a weapon from this group, he gains a +1 bonus on attack and damage rolls. Every four levels thereafter (9th, 13th, and 17th), a fighter becomes further trained in another group of weapons. He gains a +1 bonus on attack and damage rolls when using a weapon from this group. In addition, the bonuses granted by previous weapon groups increase by +1 each. For example, when a fighter reaches 9th level, he receives a +1 bonus on attack and damage rolls with one weapon group and a +2 bonus on attack and damage rolls with the weapon group selected at 5th level. Bonuses granted from overlapping groups do not stack. Take the highest bonus granted for a weapon if it resides in two or more groups. A fighter also adds this bonus to any combat maneuver checks made with weapons from this group. This bonus also applies to the fighter's Combat Maneuver Defense when defending against disarm and sunder attempts made against weapons from this group. Weapon groups are defined as follows (GMs may add other weapons to these groups, or add entirely new groups): Note from Nethys : A consolidated list of fighter weapon groups is provided here

Eldritch Guardian.class skills: The eldritch guardian adds Perception, Spellcraft, and Use Magic Device to his list of class skills, but does not gain Intimidate, Ride, or Swim as class skills.
Eldritch Guardian.familiar (ex): At 1st level, an eldritch guardian gains a familiar, treating his fighter level as his effective wizard level for the purpose of this ability. This ability replaces the bonus feat gained at 1st level.
Eldritch Guardian.share training (ex): At 2nd level, when the familiar can see and hear its master, it can use any combat feat possessed by the eldritch guardian. The familiar doesn't have to meet the feat's prerequisites, but at the GM's discretion may be precluded from using certain combat feats due to its physical form. For example, an eldritch guardian's pig familiar with access to Exotic Weapon Proficiency (spiked chain) would not gain the ability to use spiked chains, since it doesn't have any limbs capable of properly handling them. This ability replaces the bonus feat gained at 2nd level.
Eldritch Guardian.source: Familiar Folio pg. 7 Eldritch guardians are trained to detect and give warning about magic threats to the people and places they protect.
Eldritch Guardian.steel will (ex): At 2nd level, the eldritch guardian gains a +1 bonus on Will saves against fear and mind-affecting effects. This bonus increases by 1 for every 4 levels beyond 2nd. This ability replaces bravery.

combat_talent_items.description: Allies within range of this tactic are granted a +1 morale bonus on Fortitude saving throws, +1 for every 4 ranks in Diplomacy you possess, as long as they are within the natural reach of at least one other ally affected by this tactic. Once per round when an ally affected by this tactic fails a Fortitude saving throw, you may spend an immediate action to allow them to reroll the save.
combat_talent_items.name: Fortifying Phalanx

combat_talent_items.description: You can spur your allies into action to react faster to imminent threats. For the duration of this shout, you and your allies are immune to sleep and fascinated. In addition, when first affected by this shout, any sleeping allies immediately wake up, fascinated allies automatically break free of the fascinate effect, flat-footed allies no longer count as flat-footed even if they have not acted yet, and allies lying prone may stand up as an immediate action, provoking attacks of opportunity as normal.
combat_talent_items.name: Invigorating Call

combat_talent_items.description: When you use this shout, your opponents' attention is drawn to you for its duration, making it hard for them to focus on your allies. Allies within the shout's affected area may make a Stealth check to hide even if they do not have cover or concealment for the duration of the shout, but you automatically fail any Stealth checks for the shout's duration.
combat_talent_items.name: Call Attention

combat_talent_items.description: You warn your allies easier and quicker before shouting, preventing your enemies from reacting. You may warn your allies as part of a shout, rather than spending a move action. Nearby enemies do not receive a bonus on their save against your shouts when you warn your allies.
combat_talent_items.name: Advanced Notice

combat_talent_items.description: When using a shout, you may center your shout inside any square of an ongoing tactic you are maintaining, treating that square as the point of origin for that shout. If you have Breath Support or another talent or effect which would allow you to change the shape of your shout (such as into a line or cone), you choose the direction of your shout as normal from that square.
combat_talent_items.name: Projecting Voice

combat_talent_items.description: You may expend your martial focus to cause all affected enemies to attempt a Will saving throw. On a failed save, the creature loses their martial focus. This is an instantaneous effect.
combat_talent_items.name: Disarming Roar

combat_talent_items.description:
Whenever you would be affected by a magic effect that would make you unable to speak (such as the silence option of the Suppression Illusion talent), the caster must first attempt a magic skill check against a DC equal to 10 + 1/2 your Diplomacy ranks + your practitioner modifier (minimum 1). If the caster fails, your voice is not affected by the magic effect, allowing you to speak, use shouts, tactics with verbal components, etc. If the caster succeeds, your voice is completely silenced and affected by the effect normally. If the effect would suppress other forms of noise (such as moving), they still remain suppressed even if the caster fails.

Additionally, whenever the effects of your shouts would be either reduced in range or completely negated with a solid barrier or wall, they instead carry through the obstruction without interruption.
combat_talent_items.name: Piercing Voice

belts.description: this belt grants the wearer an enhancement bonus to two physical ability scores (strength, dexterity, or constitution) of +2, +4, or +6. Treat this as a temporary ability bonus for the first 24 hours the belt is worn. These bonuses are chosen when the belt is created and cannot be changed.

body.description: this dark, hooded robe has six long,  silvery, razor-sharp needles protruding from the bottom of its loose sleeves,  three on each side. The wearer can launch one needle as a ranged touch attack. The needle counts as a thrown weapon with a range increment of 10 feet. If the needle hits, it embeds itself in the target's flesh,  dealing 1 point of piercing damage and 1 point of bleed damage. A creature can pull out the needle as a full-round action, which ends the bleed effect. The needle is destroyed if an attack with it misses or when it is removed from a creature it was embedded in. The robe regrows all spent needles each morning.

chest.description: the praenomen is a two-part amulet, comprising an oval plate that covers the wearer's chest and a counterweight that hangs down the wearer's back, joined by chains. The front plate is inscribed with the cartouche of the pharaoh who is the praenomen's master; the counterweight is shaped like a cobra to honor wadjet, protector of osirion and osirion's pharaohs. The praenomen was traditionally worn by a pharaoh's royal envoy to signify that the envoy acted in the pharaoh's name and was under her protection. It grants its benefits only to loyal subjects of its masterthe pharaoh whose cartouche is inscribed upon it. The praenomen grants its wearer a +4 bonus on diplomacy and intimidate checks. Once per day, the wearer can impose a geas on another creature, compelling the target to undertake a mission for the praenomen's master. The praenomen also shields its wearer and other faithful subjects of the pharaoh from the pharaoh's enemies. Its wearer gains a +2 deflection bonus to armor class, and three times per day, the wearer can activate the praenomen to grant the benefits of heroism to all loyal subjects of its master within 30 feet. The praenomen can be rededicated to a new master by replacing the front plate and engraving the name of its new master on the cartouche, requiring a successful dc 21 craft (jewelry) check.

feet.description: slippers of scampering function in almost every way like slippers of spider climbing , except the slippers can be used for 10 rounds per day, split up as the wearer chooses (minimum 1 round per use).

hands.description: these rough leather gloves grant an enhancement bonus of +1 to +5 on attack and damage rolls with improvised weapons. Alternatively, the gloves can grant melee weapon special abilities, so long as they can be applied to melee or thrown weapons (see pages 136 137 of pathfinder rpg ultimate equipment for a list of abilities). Special abilities count as additional bonuses for determining the market value of the item, but do not modify attack or damage bonuses. Gloves of improvised might cannot have a modified bonus (enhancement bonus plus special ability bonus equivalents) higher than +5. Unlike an amulet of mighty fists , gloves of improvised might must have a +1 enhancement bonus to grant a melee weapon special ability. Normal weapons are unaffected by gloves of improvised might except when used as an improvised weapon in a way specifically permitted by the weapon such as using an arrow or bolt as a melee weapon (or if the user has an ability that allows the use of normal weapons as improvised weapons). The wearer still takes a 4 nonproficiency penalty on attack rolls with improvised weapons, as normal, unless he has the catch off-guard feat or a similar ability.

head.description: this black leather cord has a red wooden ball attached at its center. When the cord is tied around a creature's head and the wooden ball is placed in the creature's mouth, the creature cannot speak or make any vocal sounds, including verbal components of spells. When removed from the creature, the ball breaks off from the leather cord, ending the effect. A creature that is not otherwise restrained can easily untie the gag and remove it.

headband.description: adorned with stylized bronze feathers, these headbands are prized by treacherous nobles who fear an assassin's dagger in the back. While worn, an imperious headband grants its wearer a +4 deflection bonus to his ac against any attack made by a hireling, a slave, a servant, or any other sentient creature in his employ. In addition, such creatures must succeed at a dc 13 will save or treat their master as if he were affected by a sanctuary spell. If such creatures are subject to magical compulsion to attack the wearer, they must roll all attack rolls and checks to overcome spell resistance against the wearer twice and take the lower result.

contextNotes.text: Also grants one Mammoth Lords tribe sub-benefit (Bearpelt, Greattusk, Ice Chasm, Night Hunt, Raptorscale, or Slothjaw) chosen at selection — a small save/skill/speed bonus that varies by tribe.

Bloody Assault.name: Bloody Assault: Effect: melee attacks and combat maneuver checks also deal [[1d4]] bleed damage

Shield of Swings.name: Shield of Swings: full-attack with a two-handed weapon, reduce your weapon damage by [[1/2]] to gain a +[[4]] shield bonus to AC and a +[[4]] shield bonus to CMD until your next turn

feats: Extra Combat Talent (Fortifying Phalanx / Invigorating Call)
Extra Combat Talent (Call Attention / Advanced Notice)
Extra Combat Talent (Projecting Voice / Disarming Roar)

contextNotes.text: Alcoholic (major): when presented with alcohol, Will save DC [[15]] or you must drink until it is gone.

Alcoholic.description: The bottle owns you. Whenever you are presented with alcohol, you must pass a Will save (DC 15) or you are compelled to drink it, and you keep drinking until it is gone.

contextNotes.text: Illiterate: you cannot read or write any language and cannot use scrolls.

Illiterate.description: You never learned to read or write, and you refuse to learn. You cannot read or write any language, and you cannot use scrolls.

formatted_bio:
Charles Coulombe
- Alignment: Lawful Good
- Deity: Apsu
- Race: Human
- Class: Level 15 Fighter
- Archetype: Bruiser
- Tactics: Closes once, plants, and full-attacks with a two-hander every round until something dies -- usually whatever it swung at. Eats hits rather than reposition; moving costs damage and damage is the whole plan.
- Stat Focus: Str
- Disciplines: Radiant Dawn
- Homeland: Tal-falko

Vocation
- Profession: Legend of the Uncharted (rank 15)
- Profession: Dentist (rank 10)
- Profession: Master-at-Arms (rank 5)
- Profession: Upholsterer (rank 10)
- Known for: Basketweaving
- Training: An average trainer who taught them Improved Lightning Reflexes, Pikemans Training
- Training: An average trainer who taught them Powerful Throwing (combat), Darting Viper
- Training: An average trainer who taught them Flanking Specialist (combat), Bloody Assault
- Training: An average trainer who taught them Simple Weapon Proficiency, Shield of Swings

Family
- Loving Mother
- Dead Father
- Raised In A Wealthy Household
- No Siblings

Personality
- Personality: Reverent, Analytical, Doubtful
- Mannerisms: Combs mustache, Bites lower lip
- Flaws: Illiterate, Alcoholic

Appearance
- Hair: Unkempt Red
- Eyes: Grey
- Build: Defined Cheekbones

homebrew_feat_desc_dict.Bloody Assault: Sacrificing accuracy, you can inflict bloody wounds that are slow to heal
homebrew_feat_desc_dict.Combat Reflexes: You can make additional attacks of opportunity
homebrew_feat_desc_dict.Darting Viper: When using a dorn-dergar, you can quickly attack both near and distant foes
homebrew_feat_desc_dict.Death From Below: You have been trained to fight flying creatures
homebrew_feat_desc_dict.Extra Combat Talent:
Your knowledge of combat is easily expanded.

Benefit: Gain an additional sphere or a talent from a combat sphere you possess.

Special: You may take this feat multiple times. The effects stack.

homebrew_feat_desc_dict.Flanking Foil: Fighting multiple foes is easy for you
homebrew_feat_desc_dict.Flanking Specialist (combat): You are more adept at flanking with allies. you count as occupying both your current space and any space adjacent to you for the purpose of flanking an opponent (including allowing your allies to flank as if you were in any of those spaces). the space must be open; you cannot use this ability to flank from a space that contains an object, creature, or barrier.
homebrew_feat_desc_dict.Gang Up: You are adept at using greater numbers against foes
homebrew_feat_desc_dict.Hellcat Stealth: You are difficult to see in the light
homebrew_feat_desc_dict.Horn of the Criosphinx: You end your charge in a devastating two-handed attack
homebrew_feat_desc_dict.Improved Lightning Reflexes: You have a knack for avoiding danger all around you
homebrew_feat_desc_dict.Lightning Reflexes: You have faster ref lexes than normal
homebrew_feat_desc_dict.Malevolence: Your Claim carries a hindering curse. creatures claimed by you become cursed and take a 2 penalty on combat maneuver checks and skill checks for as long as they are claimed.
homebrew_feat_desc_dict.Martial Training I (Radiant Dawn): Youve learned the basics in a martial discipline. Special If you ever gain levels in a martial adept class or possess them previously, these maneuvers continue to use their own initiator level and recovery method, independent of your martial adept level. Those wishing to add new maneuvers from a discipline that is already available to their class should instead select the Advanced Study feat instead. select a martial discipline. the associated skill for this discipline is now a class skill. your initiation modifier is chosen from intelligence, wisdom, or charisma. your martial initiator level for maneuvers granted by this feat (and subsequent martial training feats) is equal to half your character level + your initiation modifier. you may select any two maneuvers from the 1st level maneuvers from this discipline, and you may ready one of your maneuvers for use. you may recover one maneuver by expending a full round action to recover it.
homebrew_feat_desc_dict.Martial Training II (Radiant Dawn): Youve continued to progress your martial studies. you may select two new maneuvers and one stance from your chosen discipline of up to 2nd level, and you may ready an additional maneuver. you must meet the minimum initiator level to select any maneuver.
homebrew_feat_desc_dict.Martial Training III (Radiant Dawn): Your mastery of your martial discipline improves. you may select an additional new maneuver from your chosen discipline of up to 3rd level, plus one new stance, and you may ready an additional maneuver. you may also trade out any one maneuver from your chosen discipline you know and replace it with a different maneuver from that discipline of up to 2nd level. you must meet the minimum initiator level to select any maneuver.
homebrew_feat_desc_dict.Martial Training IV (Radiant Dawn): You are fast approaching mastery of your chosen discipline. you may select two new maneuvers from your chosen discipline of up to 4th level, and you may ready an additional maneuver. you must meet the minimum initiator level to select any maneuver.
homebrew_feat_desc_dict.Martial Training V (Radiant Dawn): You are truly enlightened with using your chosen discipline. you may select two new maneuvers or one new maneuver and one new stance from your chosen discipline of up to 5th level, and you may ready an additional maneuver. you may also trade out any one maneuver from your chosen discipline you know and replace it with a different maneuver from that discipline of up to 4th level. you must meet the minimum initiator level to select any maneuver.
homebrew_feat_desc_dict.Martial Training VI (Radiant Dawn): You have reached your limits in mastering your chosen discipline. you may select two new maneuvers or one new maneuver and one new stance from your chosen discipline of up to 6th level, and you may ready an additional maneuver. you may also trade out any one maneuver from your chosen discipline you know and replace it with a different maneuver from that discipline of up to 5th level. you must meet the minimum initiator level to select any maneuver.
homebrew_feat_desc_dict.Multi Talented: Your profession rank cap increases by 10.
homebrew_feat_desc_dict.Multi Talented (2nd): Your profession rank cap increases by 10. This is the 2nd time you have taken this feat.
homebrew_feat_desc_dict.Opening Volley: Your ranged assault leaves your foe disoriented and vulnerable to your melee attack
homebrew_feat_desc_dict.Pikemans Training: Militaries across the land rely on lines of pikemen carrying both their long spears and a shield. You are familiar with this fighting style. you can wield a normally two-handed polearm or spear in one hand, provided you are wielding a light or heavy shield in your other hand. when wielding a weapon in this manner, you treat it in all ways as being a one-handed weapon, rather than a weapon of its normal handedness.
homebrew_feat_desc_dict.Polearm Expertise (combat): Your expertise with reach weapons lets you strike foes that are adjacent to you. Normal You cannot strike an enemy that is adjacent to you while wielding a reach weapon. as a free action, you can shorten your grip on a reach weapon that you are proficient with to use it against adjacent targets. while doing so, the weapon does not have reach, instead threatening the area for a normal melee weapon. you have a 2 penalty on attack rolls while using this feat. you can use another free action to return to the normal grip and reach.
homebrew_feat_desc_dict.Powerful Throwing (combat): Your thrown weapons are as strong as they are accurate. Special Starting at 2nd level, a ranger with the thrown weaponACG combat style may select Powerful Throwing as a combat style feat. you can use your strength modifier for both your attack and damage rolls with thrown weapons.
homebrew_feat_desc_dict.Racial Heritage: The blood of a non-human ancestor flows in your veins
homebrew_feat_desc_dict.Reckless Offense: You can shift your focus from defense to offense. when you use the attack action or full attack action in melee, you can take a penalty of 4 to your armor class and add a +2 bonus on your melee attack roll. the bonus on attack rolls and penalty to armor class last until the beginning of your next turn.
homebrew_feat_desc_dict.Shield of Swings: A wild frenzy of attacks serves to bolster your defenses
homebrew_feat_desc_dict.Simple Weapon Proficiency: You are trained in the use of basic weapons
homebrew_feat_desc_dict.Tandem Trip: You know how to work together to trip your foes
homebrew_feat_desc_dict.Tribal Scars: You endured the grueling coming-of-age rituals of your tribe or following, and proudly bear the scars that grant you the blessings of your tribe's ancestors or totem
homebrew_feat_desc_dict.True Calling: Your natural Profession rank cap rises to 15 in one qualifying profession.

contextNotes.text: Alternatively, the gloves can grant melee weapon special abilities, so long as they can be applied to melee or thrown weapons (see pages 136 137 of pathfinder rpg ultimate equipment for a list of abilities). Gloves of improvised might cannot have a modified bonus (enhancement bonus plus special ability bonus equivalents) higher than +[[5]]. The wearer still takes a 4 nonproficiency penalty on attack rolls with improvised weapons, as normal, unless he has the catch off-guard feat or a similar ability.
An imperious headband grants its wearer a +[[4]] deflection bonus to his ac against any attack made by a hireling, a slave, a servant, or any other sentient creature in his employ.

In addition, such creatures must succeed at a dc [[13]] will save or treat their master as if he were affected by a sanctuary spell. If such creatures are subject to magical compulsion to attack the wearer, they must roll all attack rolls and checks to overcome spell resistance against the wearer twice and take the lower result.

Once per day, the wearer can impose a geas on another creature, compelling the target to undertake a mission for the praenomen's master. The praenomen can be rededicated to a new master by replacing the front plate and engraving the name of its new master on the cartouche, requiring a successful dc [[21]] craft (jewelry) check. Its wearer gains a +[[2]] deflection bonus to armor class, and three times per day, the wearer can activate the praenomen to grant the benefits of heroism to all loyal subjects of its master within [[30]] feet.

unplaced: The needle counts as a thrown weapon with a range increment of 10 feet. If the needle hits, it embeds itself in the target's flesh, dealing 1 point of piercing damage and 1 point of bleed damage. A creature can pull out the needle as a full-round action, which ends the bleed effect.
Slippers of scampering function in almost every way like slippers of spider climbing , except the slippers can be used for 10 rounds per day, split up as the wearer chooses (minimum 1 round per use).

Armaments of the Empire.description: A thin layer of akasha ows forth from you and covers your and your allies weapons. While you maintain this stance, you empower a number of weapons including natural weapons within close range 25 feet + 5 feet per 2 initiator levels up to your initiation modifier. Each empowered weapon gains the benefit of a weapon special ability with a market price of +1 bonus. This ability must be chosen from the list of weapon special abilities you could normally place on a mind blade see the enhanced mind blade class feature in Chapter 3 of Ultimate Psionics or in the Reference Materials section at the end of this book. At initiator 10th and every five levels thereafter, the market price of the weapon special ability you can grant a weapon increases to +2 bonus, then +3 bonus, and so on. A weapon can only gain a single ability through this stance, though you need not grant the same ability to each aected weapon. A weapon retains its new ability for as long as it remains within close range. You choose which weapons are empowered when you enter this stance, and you can change which weapons within range are empowered as a swift action or as part of reallocating essence.

Battle Against the Sun.description: To challenge you is to challenge the sun itself: An exercise in futility. While you maintain this stance, you shed bright light, as if by a daylight spell, out to close range 25 feet + 5 feet per 2 levels. Once per round, as a free action that can be taken at any time including when it is not your turn, you may create a line with a length of 20 feet that originates anywhere within this light. Unlike normal line attacks, this line attack does not need to fire away from you; it may travel in any direction so long as the origin point is within your daylight range. Enemies within the area take damage equal to your initiator level. A successful Reflex save DC 16 + initiation modifier halves this damage. Allies caught within the line are instead healed for a number of hit points equal to your initiator level.

Curate's Strike.description: This strike was created by a kobold leader to fight both controlling magics and vicious wounds. Make an attack. If it hits, it deals weapon damage as normal, and you can heal yourself and allies within close range 25 feet + 5 feet per 2 initiator levels for a total number of hit points equal to twice your initiation modifier, divided as you choose between you and your allies. Alternatively, you may choose to grant a single ally within close range a saving throw against an ongoing effect on them that offers multiple saving throws over time to negate, or has its duration measured in rounds at the effects original DC, at the effects original DC. If it succeeds, the effect ends. This does not progress poison, diseases, or similar effects on a failed saving throw.

Decree of Silence.description: Your presence demands silence. Only those who you allow to speak may do so. You may initiate this counter in response to a creature within close range 25 feet + 5 feet per 2 initiator levels manifesting a power, casting a spell, or using a spell-like or psi-like ability. Roll damage as if youd made a successful attack with a weapon youre wielding; you dont deal this damage, but the target of this counter must succeed at a concentration check DC 10 + damage that would be dealt by this attack + the level of the spell being cast or power being manifested or lose the power, psi-like ability, spell, or spell-like ability as if it had been disrupted.

Dismiss.description: This attack softly removes an enemy from your presence. Make an attack. If it hits, you deal damage as normal, and you can make a trip attempt against the target. If your trip attempt succeeds, the target is also pushed away as if you had successfully bull rushed them, using the same result as your trip attempt. You may not move with the target with this bull rush. Neither the trip attempt nor the targets movement during the bull rush provoke attacks of opportunity. When determining your combat maneuver bonus for this strike, you may use your initiator level in place of your base attack bonus, and may choose to use your Dexterity or initiation modifer in place of your Strength modifer.

Disrupt Essence.description: A powerful blow that disrupts ones essence, inhibiting the use of abilities. Make an attack. If it hits, the target must make a Will save DC 10 + your initiation level + your initiation modifier or have a single Extraordinary Ex or supernatural Su ability that requires an action to activate, special sense, or special movement type of your choice disabled for rounds equal to your initiation modifier. You must be aware of the ability in order to disable it Such as a successful knowledge check, or having seen it in action.

Divide and Conquer.description: This strike pulls essence from the target, creating an effigy of the creature. When the essence returns to its creature, it brings its wounds with it. Make an attack. If it hits, it deals an additional 3d6 points of damage, and the target must make a Will save DC 15 + initiation modifier or have its essence drawn into one effigy until the end of your next turn. This translucent effigy appears within close range 25 feet plus 5 feet per 2 levels of you. The effigy is the size of the target of this maneuver, but otherwise does not block movement or occupy spaces, and may be targeted by attacks, spells, or other abilities. Any attack, spell, or other ability used against the effigy or including it in its aected area is redirected against the target of this maneuver as if they were the original target regardless of range, and the target may defend themselves normally against these attacks.

Healer's Bane.description: Made to combat other practitioners of the Radiant Dawn discipline, this maneuver hijacks healing for ones own purpose. You may initiate this counter in response to a target within range healing hit point damage. The target must make a will save DC 12 + initiation modifier or have their healing stolen. Instead of the target and any other creatures aected by that instance of the eect being healed, you draw the total amount of healing done into a pool, and may redistribute this pool of healing to allies within close range 25 feet + 5 feet per 2 initiator levels, divided as you choose between you and your allies. Targets that would have been healed by the healing then take damage equal to half of the healing stolen.

King's Castle.description: Your faithful respond to your call for help. You may initiate this counter in response to being attacked. One willing ally other than you teleports to a space adjacent to you and gains temporary hit points equal to your initiator level, as well as DR/ equal to your initiation modifier, both of which last for 1 round. Resolve the attack against the teleported ally instead of yourself. After the attack is resolved, the ally teleported may make a single melee or ranged attack at their highest base attack bonus against the creature that attacked you. This attack does not provoke attacks of opportunity.

Lifeburst Strike.description: You strike out with a simple blow with an uncanny power to heal and harm. Make an attack. If it hits, it deals weapon damage as normal plus an additional 1d6 points of damage, and you can heal yourself and allies within close range 25 feet + 5 feet per 2 initiator levels for a total number of hit points equal to three times your initiation modifier, divided as you choose between you and your allies. Alternatively, you may choose to grant a single ally within close range a saving throw against an ongoing eect on them that oers a saving throw to negate, at the eects original DC. If it succeeds, the eect ends. This does not progress poison, diseases, or similar eects on a failed saving throw.

Stance of the Sunlight Shield.description: This stance sits halfway between martial form and magic prowess, conjuring shields of light to defend yourself and others. While you maintain this stance, you may create sunlight shields. Creating a single sunlight shield is done as free action that can be done once per round, and is done automatically when you enter this stance. A sunlight shield can be created anywhere within close range 25 feet plus 5 feet per 2 levels of you to include in the air, where they oat until destroyed, dismissed, or removed. Treat a sunlight shield as a 10ft by 10ft by 1 inch thick wall of force, but with hardness equal to your initiator level plus your initiation modifier, and 1 hit point. They may be made smaller at the initiators discretion. You may have a number of sunlight shields equal to your initiation modifier, and these shields last indefinitely, or until they are no longer within close range of you, you dismiss them as a free action, or you leave this stance. These sunlight shields can be made at any angle, and are treated as normal terrain when stepped on. You may command these shields to y an amount of feet equal to your movement speed as a move action. You may also create a sunlight shield as an immediate action, but doing so is dangerous as the hasty construction leaves your essence tied to it. Until the start of your next turn, any damage that the shield takes before hardness is taken into account, or any spell that would fail because of the shields sudden appearance between its caster and its target is also inicted on you, regardless of distance. Creatures can attack other creatures on the other side of these shields, dealing damage to the shield first. If an attack would break the shield, the remainder of the damage is dealt to the creature if the original attack would have hit. When you enter this stance, you may designate any number of allies. These allies attacks and abilities are not impeded by your sunlight shields.

Staunching Strike.description: To help your allies and harm your enemies is the most basic tenet of the Radiant Dawn discipline. Make an attack. If it hits, it deals weapon damage as normal, and you can heal yourself and allies within close range 25 feet + 5 feet per 2 initiator levels for a total number of hit points equal to your initiation modifier, divided as you choose between you and your allies.

The Caged Sun.description: If you have 50% or fewer hit points, entering this stance can be done as a free action instead of a swift. While you maintain this stance, you cannot heal creatures other than yourself, but any healing you receive is increased by 50%. If you would be healed for more than your maximum amount of hit points, you instead gain an amount of temporary hit points equal to the excess healing. These temporary hit points stack with other temporary hit points granted by you, up to a maximum of your maximum hit points, and last for one minute, until initiative is rolled, or you abandon this stance.

profession_ability_items.description:
Profession (Legend of the Uncharted) - rank 15/15. Associate skills (ranks 1/4/7/10): Profession, Sleight of Hand, Perception, Appraise.

Martial Flexibility (Ex)

You adapt mid-fight like a brawler. As a swift action you gain the benefit of one combat feat for 1 minute (or two feats as a move action). You can use this a number of times per day equal to 3 + half your level, and the chosen feats can satisfy each other's prerequisites.

Banner of the Vanguard (Ex)

Your standard rallies those who follow you. Allies within 60 feet who can see your banner gain a +2 morale bonus on saving throws against fear and a +1 morale bonus on attack rolls made while charging; you yourself gain the same benefit.

Armor Training (Ex)

You wear armor like a second skin. Reduce your armor check penalty by 2 (minimum 0) and increase your armor's maximum Dexterity bonus by 2. The campaign treats your armor training as eight levels higher, and you move at full speed in medium armor.
profession_ability_items.name: Profession Rank 5: (Legend of the Uncharted)

profession_ability_items.description:
Profession (Legend of the Uncharted) - rank 15/15.

Warlord's Mastery (Ex)

You are a living legend of the battlefield whose every blow finds its mark. You gain an additional attack at your full base attack bonus on any full attack, a +3 untyped bonus on all attack and damage rolls, and a +3 dodge bonus to AC. Allies within 30 feet gain a +2 morale bonus on attack rolls so long as you fight.

Peerless Warrior (Ex)

You fight as a legend of the battlefield. You gain a +4 bonus on attack and damage rolls and a +2 dodge bonus to AC. Once per round when you confirm a critical hit, the target must succeed at a Fortitude save (DC 10 + half your level + your Strength modifier) or be staggered for 1 round. You treat every weapon you wield as though it had a +2 enhancement bonus.

Martial Training (initiator)

A master-at-arms taught you the secrets of a martial discipline. You become an initiator: you learn three maneuvers and one stance from a single Path of War discipline, with an initiator level equal to half your character level. You ready and recover these maneuvers as a martial adept.

Unstoppable Onslaught (Ex)

You crash through the line like a war engine. When you charge you ignore difficult terrain and the first creature in your path, and your charge attack deals an extra 2d6 damage and gains a +4 bonus to its combat maneuver check to overrun or bull rush.
profession_ability_items.name: Profession Rank 15: (Legend of the Uncharted)

profession_ability_items.description:
Profession (Dentist) - rank 10/10. Associate skills (ranks 1/4/7/10): Sense Motive, Appraise, Craft, Handle Animal.

Disease Ward (Ex)

Constant exposure to contagion has toughened your constitution. You gain a +2 resistance bonus on Fortitude saves against disease, poison, and nausea.

Battlefield Surgeon (Ex)

You work fast under fire. You can treat deadly wounds or stabilize a dying creature as a standard action rather than a full round, and on a successful Heal check a creature you stabilize regains 1 hit point.
profession_ability_items.name: Profession Rank 5: (Dentist)

contextNotes.text: +2 to attack on a whirlwind sweep of all foes in reach

profession_ability_items.description:
Profession (Master-at-Arms) - rank 5/10. Associate skills (ranks 1/4/7/10): Perception, Sleight of Hand.

Weapon Training (Ex)

Like a veteran fighter, you have mastered a whole group of weapons. You gain a +2 bonus on attack and damage rolls with weapons of your trained group; the campaign treats your effective training as eight levels higher than normal, so this bonus is already strong for your level.

Whirlwind Reach (Ex)

You sweep your weapon in a controlled arc that few can slip past. As a standard action you can make a single melee attack against every foe within reach, and you gain a +2 untyped bonus on those attack rolls.

Battle Hardened (Ex)

Countless campaigns have toughened you against punishment. You gain damage reduction 2/— against weapon attacks and a +2 bonus to your CMD against all combat maneuvers.
profession_ability_items.name: Profession Rank 5: (Master-at-Arms)

profession_ability_items.description:
Profession (Upholsterer) - rank 10/10. Associate skills (ranks 1/4/7/10): Knowledge (local), Perception, Appraise, Profession.

Master Craftsman (Ex)

You can use your Craft or Profession ranks in place of the caster-level prerequisite for item creation feats, and you craft masterwork goods in half the normal time and cost.

Sturdy Workbench (Ex)

With a proper bench, vise, and your own tools, you work without error. You gain a +2 competence bonus on Craft checks, and whenever you fail a Craft check by less than 5 while at your workbench, you do not ruin the raw materials.
profession_ability_items.name: Profession Rank 5: (Upholsterer)

profession_feat_desc.Always Improving: You can spend ordinary skill ranks in your chosen profession. (Requires True Calling and 15 ranks.)
profession_feat_desc.Multi Talented: Your profession rank cap increases by 10.
profession_feat_desc.Multi Talented (2nd): Your profession rank cap increases by 10. This is the 2nd time you have taken this feat.
profession_feat_desc.True Calling: Your natural Profession rank cap rises to 15 in one qualifying profession.

selected_traits_desc.description: You gain a +1 trait bonus to damage dealt with a dagger and a +1 trait bonus to Swim checks. Swim is always a class skill for you.
selected_traits_desc.name: River Rat

selected_traits_desc.description: You gain a +1 trait bonus on Appraise checks. Additionally, you gain a +4 bonus on Perception checks made to distinguish statue-like creatures (like caryatid columns and gargoyles) from actual sculptures.
selected_traits_desc.name: Ruin Raider

selected_traits_desc.description: You gain a +1 trait bonus on Reflex saving throws.
selected_traits_desc.name: Deft Dodger

selected_traits_desc.description: You gain a +1 trait bonus on initiative and Intimidate checks.
selected_traits_desc.name: Bloody-Minded

selected_traits_desc.description: Once per day during a combat encounter, you can choose to gain a +1 trait bonus on a single attack roll against the creature that last hit you.
selected_traits_desc.name: Vindictive Strike

selected_traits_desc.description: You gain a +1 trait bonus on Knowledge (engineering) and Knowledge (history) checks, and one of them is always a class skill for you. In addition, you may choose an ancient language as one of your bonus languages.
selected_traits_desc.name: Osirionologist

selected_traits_desc.description: You gain a +1 trait bonus on Ride checks, and Ride is always a class skill for you.
selected_traits_desc.name: Lastwall Cavalry Rider

selected_traits_desc.description: You begin play with a longsword or dueling sword and gain a +1 trait bonus on all attacks and combat maneuvers made with such weapons.
selected_traits_desc.name: Sword Scion

unlock.10: You can identify magic items without using detect magic, though the DC is increased by 10.
unlock.15: Identifying magic items is a standard action, and learning a spell takes 1 minute per spell level.
unlock.20: When attempting a caster level check, you can attempt a Spellcraft check at -20 against the same DC; success grants a +2 circumstance bonus.
unlock.5: Identifying magic items takes 1 full round, and the time to learn a spell from a spellbook is halved.

skill_unlock.unlock_html:
Spellcraft

5 Ranks: Identifying magic items takes 1 full round, and the time to learn a spell from a spellbook is halved.

10 Ranks: You can identify magic items without using detect magic, though the DC is increased by 10.

15 Ranks: Identifying magic items is a standard action, and learning a spell takes 1 minute per spell level.

20 Ranks: When attempting a caster level check, you can attempt a Spellcraft check at -20 against the same DC; success grants a +2 circumstance bonus.
